data.description:
Every VOTER_ERROR incident is counted twice by the host observability probe, doubling rebar/host:voter_errors.

Evidence (from journald on the Gerrit host, 2026-08-22, SSM read-only):
- All five VOTER_ERROR records over Aug 20-22 appear twice with IDENTICAL microsecond timestamps (e.g. two lines with timestamp 1787338223.4735096 for change Icc3bfe17..., two with 1787389627.8211215 for Id3a51812...).
- Mechanism (src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:132-148, _voter_error): the marker is emitted BOTH via logger.error("VOTER_ERROR " + json) AND via print("VOTER_ERROR " + json, file=sys.stderr). The stderr print is deliberate belt-and-braces ("so the marker lands even if logging is misconfigured" — its comment). But when logging IS configured (config.py wires a handler to stderr), both lines reach journald at line start, and the probe's anchored count (infra/scripts/observability.sh:166, grep -cE '^VOTER_ERROR \{') counts each real error twice.
- Metric confirmation: CloudWatch hourly sums show 2-3 per single-incident hour where journald shows one real error.

Impact: alarm semantics unaffected (threshold 0, any count fires), but the metric is useless for rate analysis and will mis-calibrate any future threshold (see companion recalibration task — landing that makes accuracy load-bearing).

Constraints on the fix (grounded in existing design):
- Keep the fail-safe property: the marker must still reach journald when logging is misconfigured (that is the print's documented purpose and the reason it exists).
- The token is an alarm contract (observability.sh:165 "keep this pattern in step with the emitter") — whatever changes must keep probe and emitter in lockstep, in one place if possible.
- Candidate shapes (Phase 1 decides): emit the line-start marker on exactly one path (e.g. logger line no longer matches the anchor, or print only when no handler is attached); or dedup in the probe (fragile); prefer the emitter-side single-emission.
- Sibling sweep: ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR / RECONCILE_DEGRADED / MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR markers use the same convention (reconcile.py mirrors "voter's VOTER_ERROR marker convention") — check each for the same double-emission and fix or file discovered_from.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Root cause confirmed per rebar-debug (runtime proof: drive _voter_error with configured logging and count journald-shaped lines on stderr).
- [ ] One real error produces exactly one probe-countable marker line, while the misconfigured-logging fallback still produces one.
- [ ] Sibling markers audited (fixed or ticketed).
- [ ] caused_by attributed (the dual emission shipped with the marker or with the logging-config fix in config.py — date test decides).
data.title: VOTER_ERROR marker emitted twice, doubling voter_errors metric
